topStories.headline: Masked ICE Agents Detain Man at Gunpoint on SoMa's 6th Street, Sparking City Hall Rally and $1.8M Legal Fund Push
topStories.dek: A Monday morning immigration arrest caught on home security video has set off protests, a City Hall rally, and emergency funding legislation in just four days.
topStories.body:
Security camera footage shared by a neighbor on the morning of Monday, October 19, showed as many as four U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents — some in military-style fatigues, one in plainclothes carrying a handgun — detaining a man in a navy-blue suit on 6th Street near Bessie Carmichael Elementary School during morning drop-off hours. The man, heard on video saying he was a U.S. citizen on his way to work, was pushed to the ground and led away in handcuffs.

ICE confirmed Tuesday that the man is 51-year-old Milton Ramos-Rodriguez, a Salvadoran national with a prior California voluntary manslaughter conviction who had been previously deported. Federal officials also alleged ties to the Sureños gang. Ramos-Rodriguez appeared in federal court Tuesday on a charge of illegal reentry. His sister, Claudia Melgar, told the San Francisco Standard she learned of the arrest from social media posts.

District 6 Supervisor Matt Dorsey, who represents SoMa, publicly condemned the operation on social media. The next day, Supervisor Jackie Fielder announced at a City Hall rally attended by more than 100 people — including six members of the Board of Supervisors — that the city would introduce a budget supplemental of $1.8 million for immigrant legal defense. The proposed funding would support immigration attorneys, accompaniment services for ICE appointments, and the city's rapid-response hotline. Board President Rafael Mandelman waived the standard 30-day waiting period; a vote could come as early as November 4.

The arrest intensified an already charged debate in San Francisco over federal immigration enforcement. ICE arrests in the San Francisco region have spiked nearly 70 percent year-over-year, from roughly 2,900 in the first seven months of 2025 to nearly 5,000 over the same span in 2026, according to CalMatters citing ICE records. Two ICE agents were separately spotted by public defenders in the lobby of the SF jail the same Tuesday as the rally.

topStories.headline: Dogpatch Biotech Revel Pharmaceuticals Claims a First: Reversing Molecular Aging in Human Tissue
topStories.dek: A Dogpatch longevity startup says its engineered enzyme undid a form of protein damage that scientists had considered permanent for forty years — and the results were published in Nature Communications.
topStories.body:
Revel Pharmaceuticals, a longevity startup headquartered at the American Industrial Center in Dogpatch, announced in July that its scientists — working with collaborators at Calico Life Sciences and the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus — had published results in the journal Nature Communications describing a novel engineered enzyme called CMLase. The Potrero View reported on the finding this month in a feature interview with CEO Aaron Cravens.

The enzyme targets a type of protein damage known as Nε-carboxymethyl-lysine, or CML — a compound that accumulates in the body's long-lived proteins over decades through a chemical process similar to the browning reaction that turns bread to toast. Because no human enzyme naturally reverses this buildup, it had long been considered a fixed feature of biological aging. Revel's team created CMLase through a process called directed evolution, screening more than 500 million enzyme variants to arrive at a candidate derived from a bacterial scaffold.

When tested on human tissue from donors aged 20 to 75, the enzyme reduced CML levels by more than 70 percent in arterial tissue from a 75-year-old donor, and by more than 55 percent in aged donor skin — bringing that skin sample's molecular markers to levels typically seen in 31-year-old skin. The enzyme left the underlying proteins intact throughout. The findings open a potential path toward treatments for inflammatory conditions linked to aging, including heart and kidney disease, arthritis, and cataracts. Cravens told the Potrero View and Chemistry & Engineering News that significant further work is needed before any clinical application.

topStories.headline: Teen Fatally Shot at Potrero Hill Terrace and Annex, Second Gun Violence Incident This Year at the Redeveloping Complex
topStories.dek: A teenager was killed Friday evening at the Potrero Hill public housing project, which is currently being torn down and rebuilt as a mixed-income development.
topStories.body:
San Francisco police responded Friday evening, October 17, to a shooting at the Potrero Hill Terrace and Annex housing complex, where a teenager was killed, according to Mission Local. The San Francisco Police Department confirmed the fatality. No further details about the victim or a suspect were released publicly as of this week.

The shooting is the second this year at the approximately 600-unit complex on the eastern slope of Potrero Hill, which is in the active process of being demolished and rebuilt as a mixed-income residential site. The Potrero Annex Terrace is one of the last remaining traditional public housing complexes in San Francisco; its redevelopment has been underway for several years and is expected to dramatically change the character of the site once complete.

The killing adds to ongoing concerns about public safety at the complex during its extended transition period. Community advocates have raised questions about whether demolition-era disruption and resident displacement have contributed to instability at the site. The redevelopment is managed through a public-private partnership and is tied to the city's broader effort to replace aging housing stock with mixed-income buildings.

moreNews.headline: Thrill-O-Ween Cancelled at Mission Bay's Thrive City — Valkyries WNBA Finals to Blame
moreNews.body: Thrive City's sixth annual Thrill-O-Ween family Halloween celebration, scheduled for Saturday, October 24, has been cancelled due to scheduling conflicts created by the Golden State Valkyries' run in the 2026 WNBA Finals. Chase Center's official events page posted the cancellation notice this week, noting that the Halloween event — which was to have featured trick-or-treat stations, a pumpkin patch, a costume contest, and an outdoor screening of E.T. — could not proceed alongside Finals operations at the adjacent arena. Thrive City says it will announce additional free holiday programming for November and December.

moreNews.headline: Mission Bay Block 4 East Scores Building Permits for 398 Affordable Homes in Two-Tower Plan
moreNews.body: Building permits were issued in early October for both phases of Mission Bay Block 4 East, a 100-percent-affordable housing development at 3rd Street between Mission Rock Street and China Basin Street. Developers Curtis Development and Bayview Senior Services plan a 16-story tower at 506 China Basin Street with 165 apartments (Phase One) and a 23-story tower at 505 Mission Rock Street with 233 apartments (Phase Two), for a combined 398 units ranging from one to four bedrooms. The project is designed by Perry Architects and Y.A. Studio, with construction estimated to cost just over $125 million. A completion timeline has not been announced.
